answer_1.quote: In this paper, we propose the Scribendi Score, which is a reference-less metric to evaluate GEC system outputs that strongly correlates with human judgement. We use the output of the 12 systems evaluated in CoNLL-2014's shared tasks for GEC. The test set consists of 1312 sentences.

answer_2.quote: We use GPT-2 without further fine tuning to measure the perplexity of a source and predictions from different models... We use a token sort ratio and a Levenshtein distance ratio to assess syntactic similarity and combine them into the Scribendi Score.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT-2 without further fine tuning to measure the perplexity of a source and predictions from different models. If the perplexity score improves (i.e., decreases), then we check whether the predicted sentences are syntactically related to the source sentence.

answer_4.quote: Following the CoNLL-2014 shared task on grammatical error correction ... and simultaneously performed a human evaluation of the system outputs. Human-to-human Pearson correlation for ranking the 12 different system outputs is 0.73 ≤ r ≤ 0.81.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters ranked the system outputs to produce a quality ranking.
